The research was carried out by Imperial College London, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust and the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust and is published in Osteoporosis International.

items.title: Paxlovid tied to 12% lower risk of long COVID in high-risk adults
items.text: Adults at high risk for severe COVID-19 who were prescribed nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) within five days of infection were less likely to be hospitalized or die in the next six months than those who weren't given the antiviral drug, according to a large study published in PLOS Global Public Health. For patients at low risk for severe outcomes, the results were inconclusive.
